2. The prosecution's case as revealed from the police report is as under:-
2.1 The victim aged 15 years was residing with her parents and elder sister.
On 17/11/2018, she left her house by telling that, she was going to purchase the clothes.
However, she did not return home.
The victim was in the habit of going out and returning back.
The victim's mother took search of the victim.
When the victim was not found, she lodged a missing report with the police on 28/11/2018.
2.2 After some days, the victim went to the house of her elder sister at Madna Jalalkheda.
Her sister made a phone call to her parents and informed them about the victim.
The parents went there and brought the victim.
The victim informed the parents that, for purchasing the medicines for piles, she Rajesh S/O. Kisanji Tagade vs State Of Mah. Thr. Pso, Ps Midc, Nagpur ...

At Katol, she met with the Appellant and his wife.
They both took her to their house.
She stayed there for some days.
There, the Appellant did sexual intercourse with the victim.

The Appellant took the victim with him to his sister's 4 CRI.APEAL 406-2023-J.odt house,
where again he did sexual intercourse with the victim.
The Appellant and the victim stayed there for 2-3 days.
From there, the Appellant, the victim, the husband of Appellant's sister and two other persons went to the Tahsil Office, where the victim was asked to sign on a stamp paper.
The victim signed.
They returned back to the house of the Appellant.
Thereafter, the victim went to her sister's house.
2.3 The Crime bearing No. 0598/2018 came to be registered with the MIDC Police Station, Nagpur City.

The Sections 376(2)(i)(o) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short, 'IPC') and Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (for short, 'POCSO Act') came to be added to the aforesaid Crime Number, which was initially registered for the offence of kidnapping.

sentences.text: The statement of the victim was recorded and she was referred for medical examination.
The Appellant came to be arrested and he was sent for medical examination.
The spot panchanama was done.
The Statement of the witnesses were recorded.
Necessary samples of the victim and that of the Appellant were taken.
On completion of investigation, the Appellant came to be charge-sheeted.
5 CRI.APEAL 406-2023-J.odt 2.4

The learned Trial Court framed the Charge against the Appellant vide Exh.4 for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 376(2)(i)(j)(n) of the IPC and for the offence punishable under Sections 4 and 6 of the POCSO Act, and framed the additional Charge vide Exh. 83 for the offence punishable under Section 376(3) of the IPC.
The Appellant pleaded not-guilty and came to be tried.

To prove the charge, the prosecution examined in all ten (10)
witnesses and brought on record the relevant documents.
2.5 After the prosecution filed the evidence closure pursis, the learned Trial Court recorded the statement of the Appellant under Section 313(1)(b) of the Cr.P.C.
The Appellant denied the evidence and case of the prosecution.
On appreciating the evidence available on record, the learned Trial Court passed the impugned judgment and order convicting and sentencing the Appellant as above.
3. Heard the learned Advocate for the Appellant, the learned APP for the State and the learned Advocate for the victim.
Scrutinized the evidence available on record.
6 CRI.APEAL 406-2023-J.odt 4.

When the charge is for the penal Sections of the POCSO Act, it becomes necessary for the prosecution to establish that, the victim was a child as defined under Section 2(d) of the POCSO Act i.e. below 18 years of age.
To prove the age of the victim, the prosecution relies on the testimony of the victim who is examined as P.W.-1.
Though the victim deposed her date of birth, it would be inadmissible being hearsay.
The victim's evidence shows that, the Birth Certificate below Exh.12 was brought on record.
The said Birth Certificate is dated 19/12/2018, which is admittedly after registration of the crime.
No witness in support of said Exh.12 is examined by the prosecution to prove its authenticity.

The evidence of P.W.10 - Purushottam D. Nakat, who conducted the initial investigation shows that, there was no document on record to show that, he obtained the Birth Rajesh S/O. Kisanji Tagade vs State Of Mah. Thr. Pso, Ps Midc, Nagpur ... on 26 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52727810/
3 Certificate vide Exh. 12 from the father of the victim.
His evidence shows that, he did not verify the genuineness of Exh.12 - Birth Certificate from the concerned office.
The suggestion is given that, the said certificate was false.
Under such circumstances, the said Exh.12 cannot form the basis to prove the date of birth of the victim.
7 CRI.APEAL 406-2023-J.odt 5.
The evidence of the victim P.W. 1 shows that, the 'Hamipatra' below Exh. 13 was brought on record.
The said document was confronted to P.W.-9 Jivan Dhonduji Bhatkule who conducted the investigation after the papers of a part investigation was handed over to him.
It has come in his evidence that, Exh.13 'Hamipatra' was signed by the victim along with others and in the said 'Hamipatra', the age of the victim was written as 18 years.

Even if Exh.13 'Hamipatra' is ignored, on the basis of victim's evidence that, it was not read over to her, there is no credible evidence on the record to conclusively prove the date of birth of the victim and that the victim was a child at the time of offence.
The mother of victim though was examined as P.W.-2, she nowhere deposed of the date of birth of the victim.

Though it was possible for the prosecution to lead the evidence from the school of the victim, where she studied upto 7th standard, as seen from the evidence of the victim,
no such evidence is brought on record by the prosecution.
The prosecution thus, failed to establish that, the victim was a child at the relevant time.
6. The prosecution's case largely rests on the testimony 8 CRI.APEAL 406-2023-J.odt of the victim.
The victim's testimony shows that, on 17/11/2018, she left her house at 11.00 a.m. by saying that, she was going to purchase the clothes.
For the problem of 'piles', she wanted to purchase the medicines.
She came to Nagpur Bus Stand and from there, proceeded for Katol, where the person selling the medicines was residing.
In the afternoon, she reached the Katol Bus Stop, where she met the Appellant and his wife.
The victim enquired with them about the address of the said person from whom she wanted to purchase the medicine.
She was told that, the shop was closed.
The Appellant and his wife took the victim to their house.
As the victim was asked by the Appellant's wife to stay at their house, she stayed there for whole night.
On the next day, the victim told the Appellant's wife to allow her to stay there as she was afraid of her parents.
On 19/11/2018, the Appellant's wife went for work and her son went to school, so the victim was alone in the house.
At that time, the Appellant expressed his liking for her and told her that, he wanted to marry her.
The Appellant removed her clothes and did sexual intercourse.
When she shouted, the Appellant pressed her mouth and threatened to kill her.
The victim remained silent.
On the next day, the Appellant took the victim to his sister's house and told his sister 9 CRI.APEAL 406-2023-J.odt that, he would perform the marriage with the victim.
The Appellant did sexual intercourse with the victim at the place of his sister, where they stayed for 2-3 days.
The Appellant's brother-in-law (sister's husband) and two persons took the victim to the Tahsil Office and took her signature on a stamp paper at Exh.13.
Thereafter, they all came back to the house of the Appellant.
From there, the victim came to the house of her sister at Madna Jalalkheda.
The victim's sister made a phone call to the parents and victim's parents came there and took her to Nagpur.
Her statement was recorded by the Police and by the Magistrate.

sentences.text: 4 7. The above evidence of the victim clearly shows that, she left her house on her own.
Even the evidence of P.W.-2 victim's mother shows that, the victim left the house by saying that, she was going for purchasing the clothes.
It is clear from the victim's testimony that, she travelled alone by bus from Nagpur to Katol.
Her evidence shows that, she requested the Appellant and his wife to allow her to stay at their house and as they permitted, she stayed with them.
It has come in the cross- examination of the victim that, she knew one boy named Sahil.
With the phone of the Appellant, she made a call to the said 10 CRI.APEAL 406-2023-J.odt Sahil.
She was knowing the said Sahil from last six (6) months.
Her evidence shows that, she used to talk with the said Sahil on phone.
She made a phone call to Sahil twice on that day, but Sahil did not pick up the phone.
Suggestions was given that, she was having love affair with the said Sahil.

Her evidence shows that,
she herself asked the mobile phone of the Appellant and made a phone call to Sahil.
8. The above discussed evidence of the victim shows that, the victim was a courageous girl.
Though the victim was subjected to sexual intercourse against her wish by the Appellant, she neither informed about the same to the Appellant's wife, nor to the sister of the Appellant, nor anyone.
It is not that the victim was in captivity.
She had all the opportunity to disclose about the act of the Appellant committed with her.

Her silence and staying willingly in the house of the Appellant,
makes her evidence in respect of forceful sexual intercourse doubtful.
The victim cannot be said to be a truthful witness.
The reasonable inference which can be drawn from the testimony of the victim is that, the possibility of having consensual sexual intercourse with the Appellant cannot be ruled out.
The victim's version of rape and 11 CRI.APEAL 406-2023-J.odt penetrative sexual assault by the Appellant on her, appears doubtful.
9. There is medical evidence on record of P.W.-6 Dr. Anamika Sing who was the Medical Officer at the Government Medical College and Hospital, Nagpur.

entities.text: Government Medical College and Hospital, Nagpur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Her evidence shows that, she examined the victim and found the Hymen injury present and position of tears was 3-9 O clock.
No external injury was found on the victim at the time of medical examination.
Undisputedly, the medical examination of the victim was done after a period of three (3) weeks from the incident.

When the victim's testimony is not found to be credible, the said medical evidence will not be sufficient to hold that,
the Charge was proved.

Though the evidence of the victim shows that, she came to know the name of the Appellant and his wife when she went to the house of the Appellant, she did not disclose the name of the Appellant in the history given to the P.W.-6 the Medical Officer who deposed that, while giving the history of the assault, the victim didn't name the person.

The Chemical Analyzer Report (CA report) at Exh. 20 shows that, the blood group of the Appellant was 'O' and the CA report below Exh.
12 CRI.APEAL 406-2023-J.odt 20A in respect of knicker and underwear shows the blood group 'A',
and therefore, it will not be incriminating.
The other evidence on record do not take the prosecution's case any further in establishing the Charge.

10. The evaluation of the evidence available on record as discussed above shows that, the prosecution failed to establish that, the victim was a child at the relevant time and the sexual intercourse by the Appellant with the victim, was without her consent.
The prosecution's evidence is not conclusive to prove the Charge.

The Appeal succeeds.

Hence, the following order:-
13 CRI.APEAL 406-2023-J.odt ORDER I) The Criminal Appeal is allowed.
II) The conviction and sentence awarded by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Nagpur against the Appellant in Special (POCSO) Case No. 105 of 2019, by the impugned judgment and order dated 26/04/2023, is hereby quashed and set aside.
III) The Appellant is acquitted for the offences punishable under Sections 4 and 6 of the POCSO Act and Sections 363, 376(3), 376(2)(j) & (n) of the IPC.
IV) The Appellant is behind the bars.
He be set at liberty, if not required in any other offence.
V) The fine amount, if any, paid by the Appellant, be refund to him.
VI) Record and Proceedings be sent back to the learned Trial Court.

VII) The fees of the learned Advocate appointed to represent the Respondent no. 2 - Victim is quantified at Rs. 7,500/- [Rupees Seven Thousand Five Hundred Only], which shall be paid by the High Court Legal Services Sub-Committee, Nagpur.
